strings.note: Rubber stamp struck across the star row at the foot of the day-end tape on a zero-star night. Heavy face 24 px, 226 px inside the stamp's frame, one line, about 10 characters.
Rubber stamp struck across the star row at the foot of the day-end tape when tonight beat every earlier night. Heavy face 24 px, 258 px inside the stamp's frame, one line, about 11 characters.

Fallback name for a critic row on the day-end slip when the customer has no name. ONLY THE FIRST WORD is shown, in capitals (English shows "A"), so put the word that should show first. Body face 16 px.
Why a critic scored as they did, printed in quiet ink after their first name on the day-end slip: the player threw them out. Lower case, one short line, ~16 characters (the name shares the row).
Critic reason on the day-end slip: the customer left angry before being served. Lower case, ~16 characters.
Critic reason on the day-end slip: they were poured a different drink than they asked for. Lower case, ~16 characters.
Critic reason on the day-end slip: the drink landed perfectly. Lower case, ~16 characters.
Critic reason on the day-end slip: the drink was decent. Lower case, ~16 characters.
Critic reason on the day-end slip: the drink was poorly made. Lower case, ~16 characters.
Reason for a fine in dayend.bill.fines: the customer was served on a cheap reprinted ID. Capitals, ~14 characters.
Reason for a fine in dayend.bill.fines: the customer was served on an ID drawn by hand. Capitals, ~16 characters.
Reason for a fine, filling {reason} in dayend.bill.fines: an under-age customer was served. Several reasons may be listed joined by ", ". Capitals, ~14 characters.
Reason for a fine in dayend.bill.fines: the customer was served on someone else's ID card. Capitals, ~14 characters.
Reason for a fine in dayend.bill.fines: the customer was served on a doctored ID card. Capitals, ~14 characters.
Reason for a fine in dayend.bill.fines: a minor was served without their ID card being checked. Capitals, ~14 characters.
Fallback reason for a fine in dayend.bill.fines when no specific reason applies. Capitals, ~14 characters.

Quiet line under MALIBU CLUB at the head of the day-end tape. {served} = customers served, {walked} = customers who walked out or were wrongly shown out (whole numbers, often two digits). Small line, centred on the tape's 392 px column, about 26 characters.
Caption on the head of THE WEEK card under the day-end week hook; the week number sits at its right. Body face 16 px, about 16 characters.
Line on THE WEEK card: what the week has taken so far, tonight included (hidden on the week's first night). A money figure sits at the right. Body face 16 px, about 18 characters.
Line on THE WEEK card: the week's profit or loss so far, tonight included (hidden on the week's first night). A signed money figure sits at the right. Body face 16 px, about 18 characters.
Under the standing gauge on the TOMORROW board: the bar's star standing before tonight. {stars} is a two-decimal number like 3.25. Body face 16 px, about 12 characters.
Chip beside WAS on the TOMORROW board when tonight did not move the bar's standing (otherwise it shows +0.12 / -0.12). Display face 16 px in a 104 px box, about 6 characters.
Rate row on the day-end tape, left of five hearts and a two-decimal figure: tonight's drinks rating. Body face 16 px (the small line where the house face is handed on), about 12 characters.
Rate row on the day-end tape, left of five medallions and a two-decimal figure: tonight's room rating. Body face 16 px (the small line where the house face is handed on), about 12 characters.
Second crowd row on the TOMORROW board when tomorrow's crowd differs from tonight's: tonight's crowd name sits at its right. Body face 16 px, about 12 characters.
Caption on the head of the day-end TOMORROW board; the next night's name sits at its right in cyan. Body face 16 px, about 12 characters.

Caption on the head of the day-end TOMORROW board on the night whose dawn shuts the bar for good (third night in a row closed in debt), in place of TOMORROW; dayend.stand.closes sits at its right in red. Body face 16 px, about 12 characters.

Red reading at the right of AT DAWN on the TOMORROW board's head, on the night that ends the run: the bar will not open again. Display face 16 px; caption and reading share one 336 px line, so about 18 characters.

strings.text: EVERY RUNG ON THE LADDER IS OPEN
strings.note: One line on the TOMORROW board where the next rung would be, when no rung is left to climb. Body face 16 px, wraps, two lines of about 24 characters.

strings.text: {n} THING IS STILL IN THE BASKET.
strings.note: Warning in the 'close the order?' dialog on the market tablet when leaving with unbought items. {n} is the number of items. Shop bold face 16 px, wraps in 540 px, ~2 lines.

strings.text: {n} THINGS ARE STILL IN THE BASKET.
strings.note: As dayend.closing.basket#one.
Warning in the 'close the order?' dialog when the player bought nothing tonight. Shop bold face 16 px, wraps in 540 px, ~2 lines.
Title bar of the Windows-98 style 'are you sure' dialog on the market tablet. Shop bold face 16 px, one line in 592 px.
Safe key in the 'close the order?' dialog: return to the market. Shop bold face 16 px on a 240 px key, ~14 characters.
Key in the 'close the order?' dialog: leave the market and open tomorrow regardless. Shop bold face 16 px on a 240 px key, ~14 characters.
Aisle heading on the market's restock page. Shop sign band, one line, ~24 characters.
Aisle heading on the market's restock page (kegs). Shop sign band, one line, ~24 characters.
Aisle heading on the market's restock page. Shop sign band, one line, ~24 characters.
Aisle heading on the market's restock page. Shop sign band, one line, ~24 characters.
Aisle heading on the market's restock page. Shop sign band, one line, ~24 characters.
Aisle heading on the market's restock page for anything that fits no other aisle. Shop sign band, one line, ~24 characters.
Title line over the market tablet after the day-end slip. One line.
Key under the day-end slip that moves on to the market (the author, 2026-09-25: "devam et" - the same word as build.bill.continue). One line on the key.

The same key under the day-end slip on the night that shuts the bar for good: it skips the market and goes to the end of the run (a padlock is drawn beside the word). Imperative, like closing a bar for the night. Body face 16 px, one line on a 300 px key with a 32 px mark, about 14 characters.
Block heading on the day-end slip over the income lines. Body face 16 px, quiet ink.
Bill row label on the day-end slip, body face 24 px, money figure at the right; the label column is ~62% of the 384 px sheet, ~14 characters.
Bill row label on the day-end slip, body face 24 px, ~14 characters.
Bill row label on the day-end slip: the reward for rightly throwing out customers who should not be served. {n} is how many were shown out. Body face 24 px, ~22 characters.
As dayend.bill.thanks#one.

Bill row label on the day-end slip: what the hostess paid tonight for a job done. {who} = her first name in capitals, from the cast file (never write a name here). Body face 24 px, money figure at the right, ~14 characters.
Block heading on the day-end slip over the expense lines. Body face 16 px, quiet ink.
Bill row label on the day-end slip, body face 24 px, red ink, ~14 characters.
Bill row label on the day-end slip: bottles and restocks bought. Body face 24 px, ~14 characters.
Bill row label on the day-end slip: upgrades bought for the bar. Body face 24 px, ~14 characters.
Bill row label on the day-end slip for fines from the law. {reason} is one or more of the dayend.fine.* words joined by ", ". Body face 24 px, ~30 characters.
Heavy bill row on the day-end slip: tonight's profit or loss. Display face 16 px, ~10 characters.
Heavy bill row on the day-end slip: money in the till after tonight. Display face 16 px, ~10 characters.
Red band closing THE WEEK card beside the day-end tape when the till is in debt. {strikes} = red nights so far, {limit} = red nights that close the bar. Body face 16 px, 312 px, wraps to two lines.

strings.text: one more red day closes the bar
strings.note: Second line of the red band on THE WEEK card when one more night in debt ends the run. Lower case, body face 16 px, 312 px, wraps.

strings.text: that was the last one: the bar closes at dawn
strings.note: Second line of the red band on THE WEEK card on the night that ends the run (the band's first line then reads STRIKE 3/3): tonight was the last red night the bar could take. Lower case, body face 16 px, 312 px, wraps to two lines.

Second line of the counterfoil torn off the day-end tape and hung on the week's hook. {n} = the night number, three digits; "Z" is a till's end-of-day report, keep it. Body face 16 px, 196 px of room, 8 characters at most.

Red row on the day-end tape: money paid back for drinks that never came, {n} = how many walked out before their drink. Body face 24 px (16 when long), a money figure at its right, about 16 characters.
As dayend.tape.walkouts#one.
Caption on the day-end TOMORROW board over the next rung's title; the rung's star gate is drawn beside it as stars and a figure. Body face 16 px, 14 characters at most.
Under the next rung's title on the TOMORROW board: how many things the rank certificate will list when the bar reaches it. {n} is a whole number. Body face 16 px, 312 px, about 24 characters.
As dayend.tomorrow.opens#one.

Red line on the TOMORROW board when the room's comfort capped tonight's stars below what the customers gave. {stars} = the cap, two decimals like 3.40. Body face 16 px, wraps to two lines of about 24 characters.
As dayend.tomorrow.room_held, when the menu (the drinks served) capped tonight's stars. {stars} two decimals.
Caption on the TOMORROW board beside the name of tomorrow's crowd (REGULARS, HIGH ROLLERS...) and an arrow when it changed. Body face 16 px, 14 characters at most.
The hostess's job on the TOMORROW board, finished tonight; set in lime beside the job's picture. Body face 16 px, 10 characters at most.

The hostess's job on the TOMORROW board when its goal is met and the dawn will pay it (a rung, the room, a fitting). {reward} is digits only. Body face 16 px, lime, about 22 characters, wraps in 236 px.
Lamp note at the end of the market's department bar: one upgrade can still be fitted tonight. One line, ~18 characters.
Lamp note at the end of the market's department bar: tonight's upgrade is already taken. One line, ~18 characters.
Heading of the market basket when it is empty. One line, ~12 characters.
Heading of the market basket with {n} items in it. One line, ~12 characters.
As dayend.basket.head_count#one.
Clock corner of the market tablet's desktop. {day} is the run's night number. One line, ~8 characters.
Aisle heading at the top of the market's restock page, over the whole-well tile. Shop sign band, one line, ~24 characters.
Name on the market tile that refills every bottle at once. Tile name, ~24 characters.
Small line under the whole-well tile's name. ~24 characters.
Heading of the reading card for the whole-well tile. Capitals, one line.
Line under the heading of the whole-well reading card. One line.

strings.text: Fills every bottle behind the bar. {price} per measure.
strings.note: Description on the whole-well reading card. {price} is a price with its currency sign, like $3. Wraps.

strings.text: {price} a measure · {total} for the bottles not already in the basket
strings.note: Cost line on the whole-well reading card when some bottles are already picked singly. {price} = price per measure with its currency sign ($3); {total} = the order's total as a bare number. Wraps.

strings.text: {price} a measure · {total} to fill the shelf
strings.note: Cost line on the whole-well reading card. {price} = price per measure with its currency sign ($3); {total} = the order's total as a bare number. Wraps.

strings.text: Tops up every bottle below that you have not picked yourself
strings.note: Benefit line on the whole-well reading card. Wraps.
State word on a restock tile whose bottles are already covered by the basket. 2 capitals in a 66 px slot — keep it very short.
State word on a restock tile whose bottle (or whole shelf) needs nothing. 4 capitals at most.
State row word on the whole-well tile when every short bottle is already in the basket. 6 capitals at most (the row keeps 44 units for its reading).

strings.text: Every bottle that needs filling is already in the basket.
strings.note: Line on the whole-well reading card when there is nothing left for it to add. Wraps.

strings.text: Nothing to pour away — every bottle is at the brim.
strings.note: Line on the whole-well reading card when every bottle is full. Wraps.

strings.text: Covered by the whole-well order — no need to buy it twice
strings.note: Line on a single bottle's reading card when the whole-well order already refills it. Wraps.
Aisle heading on the market's liquor page (tonight's bottles for sale). Shop sign band, one line, ~24 characters.
Aisle heading on the market's mixer page. Shop sign band, one line, ~24 characters.
Aisle heading on the market's liquor page over the beer kegs. Shop sign band, one line, ~24 characters.
Aisle heading on the market's mixer page over the garnishes. Shop sign band, one line, ~24 characters.
Line under the heading of a bottle's reading card when the bottle is new stock tonight. {meta} is the bottle's usual description line (style, origin...). One line where possible.
State word on a market tile already bought tonight. 4 capitals at most.
Aisle heading on the market's recipe page. Shop sign band, one line, ~24 characters.
Name on a recipe tile that is still locked (the drink's name is hidden on purpose). Tile name, ~24 characters.
Small line under a locked recipe tile's name. ~24 characters.
Heading of the reading card for a locked recipe. Capitals, one line.

strings.text: The house will not open this one for you yet
strings.note: Line under the heading of a locked recipe's reading card. One line where possible.
Line under the heading of a recipe's reading card. {difficulty} = the drink's difficulty word, {prep} = how it is made (shaken, stirred...), {glass} = the glass's name. One line where possible.

strings.text: On the menu tomorrow — one more drink to sell
strings.note: Benefit line on a buyable recipe's reading card. Wraps.
Line on a buyable recipe's reading card. {difficulty} is the drink's difficulty word. One line.
Name on the sealed tile at the end of the recipe page: how many recipes are still locked. {n} is the count. Tile name, ~24 characters.
As dayend.more.name#one.

strings.text: {n} line the van will not bring you yet
strings.note: Line under the heading of the 'more waiting' reading card on a market page: {n} items still locked. One line where possible.

strings.text: {n} lines the van will not bring you yet
strings.note: As dayend.more.lines#one.

strings.text: {n} drink the house will not open for you yet
strings.note: Line under the heading of the 'more waiting' reading card on the recipe page: {n} recipes still locked. One line where possible.

strings.text: {n} drinks the house will not open for you yet
strings.note: As dayend.more.drinks#one.
Heading of the 'more waiting' reading card. {stars} is a one-decimal star rating like 3.5. Capitals, one line.

strings.text: Get {stars} stars and more of these show up here.
strings.note: Description on the 'more waiting' reading card. {stars} is a one-decimal star rating like 3.5. Wraps.
Warning line on the 'more waiting' reading card. {stars} = the rating needed, {have} = the bar's current rating, both one-decimal numbers like 3.5. One line.
Name on the placeholder tile of an empty market page. Tile name, ~24 characters.
Small line under the empty-page tile's name. ~24 characters.
Heading of the reading card for the empty-page tile. Capitals, one line.

strings.text: The van brings a different list every night
strings.note: Line under the heading of the empty-page reading card. One line where possible.

strings.text: What it brings depends on what you already have, and on how many stars you have.
strings.note: Description on the empty-page reading card. Wraps.
Title bar of the host's message box on the market tablet when the host has no name to show. Shop bold face 16 px, one line.
Key in the host's message box on the market: show her next line. Shop bold face 16 px on a 240 px key, ~14 characters.
Key in the host's message box on the market, on her last line: close the box. Shop bold face 16 px on a 240 px key, ~14 characters.

strings.text: Comes with the bar spoon — from then on the tin can be stirred, not only shaken.
strings.note: Extra sentence on a stirred recipe's market card while the bar has no bar spoon yet: buying the first stirred recipe puts the spoon on the bench. Wraps.
